transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-23 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Noah Rivera (Redwood CSM); Lena Ortiz (Sundance Eng Lead), Mark Duval (Sundance Product), Priya Shah (Sundance Infra), plus one contractor listed as Speaker 1

Summary:
Quick kickoff to align success criteria for a pilot (3-4 week) to evaluate unit economics for an LLM-powered content suggestion feature. Focus on per-token cost estimates, latency SLOs, batching and prefix/KV cache opportunities, and a small benchmark plan. Customer has strict monthly budget cap and 99th latency target for interactive UI.

Topics covered:
- Current architecture and proxies
- Expected traffic shape (burst vs steady)
- Token counts and prompt/response length distributions
- Cost levers: batching, caching, quantization variants, routing to cheaper model variants for degraded mode
- Bench plan and telemetry needs
- Timeline and next steps

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: okay thanks everyone for joining, we are live, quick intros?
[00:04] Lena: hey lena ortiz, eng lead at sundance, focusing on our newsroom product, nice to meet you all
[00:08] Mark: mark, product, want to make sure latency is tight for editors
[00:12] Priya: priya infra, i'll own network and security questions
[00:15] Maya: great, arjun on the line?
[00:17] Arjun: yep arjun patel, se, i'll run the bench and help design the POC sizing
[00:22] Noah: noah here, csm, i'll help coordinate timelines and success criteria
[00:25] Speaker 1: contractor here, doing the data shaping work

[00:30] Maya: high level - goal is a 3 week pilot to prove we can hit editor 95th latency under 400ms on median requests and keep cost under $X per month. i'm being intentionally vague on X because lena you'll tell us budget?
[00:42] Lena: yes we've got a hard cap of about $12k monthly for this feature while in pilot/proof. production budget may be higher but for this pilot we want to see realistic per-token numbers and extrapolated run rates.
[00:55] Mark: and from product, if 95th is under 500ms we can put it behind a beta flag, 400ms is aspirational.
[01:02] Arjun: ok good. quick clarifying q: are you mostly interactive single-turn prompts from editors, or multi-turn chat sessions?
[01:09] Lena: mostly single-turn suggestion prompts, average prompt length about 45 tokens and we expect reply ~120 tokens, but there are outliers.
[01:16] Speaker 1: there are long-form generation cases too when they ask for full paragraph drafts, those push to 600-800 tokens occasionally
[01:22] Maya: perfect, that distribution helps. for cost modeling we break into typical (45/120) and heavy write (45/600).

[01:30] Arjun: let's talk about the cost knobs -- batching, kv/prefix cache, quantization and routing to cheaper model sibling. on Redwood we can profile 3 modes: high-quality float16 8k model (higher token cost), int8/4 quant variant (lower cost, ~30-45% token cost savings for throughput), and a low-cost 3B variant for degraded mode.
[01:48] Priya: what's the expected latency impact of quantization? we worry quantized runs could hurt tail latency.
[01:55] Arjun: good call. quantized kernels often improve throughput and can slightly improve median latency, but for 99th you need to watch batching behavior; small batch sizes still dominate the kernel overhead. we'll instrument p50/p95/p99. also the KV cache matters a lot for prompt-heavy workloads if you have prefix reuse across requests.
[02:12] Mark: prefix reuse? can you spell that out?
[02:14] Arjun: sure - if editors prepend the same prompt scaffold (e.g., article metadata), KV/prefix cache can avoid re-computing early tokens. effective hit rates translate into big token savings. even 20% cache hit can lower token spend materially.
[02:26] Lena: we have a canonical header for article context that is used most of the time, so i'd expect decent prefix reuse maybe 30-40%

[02:36] Maya: budget wise with $12k/month, if we assume 45/120 typical and call volume of 25k requests/mo, rough math: tokens per request ~165 => 4.125M tokens/mo. at say $0.0035 per 1k tokens that's about $14.4 — wait this math is messy on the call but we will send a spreadsheet.
[02:59] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[03:02] Lena: we need the per-1k token basis, also show how batching reduces cost per token with example batch sizes for our latency constraints.

[03:10] Arjun: absolutely, our bench will sweep batch sizes 1,2,4,8 and simulate your latency SLO to show cost vs p95. we'll also run scenarios with and without prefix caching. expect token-level pricing differences between model variants and quantization.
[03:24] Mark: what about steady vs burst? our publish windows spike when headlines drop.
[03:28] Maya: we recommend reserving a small dedicated pool for predictable baseline and allowing burst to shared capacity. Dedicated gives predictable throughput; reserved cost is monthly commitment. For a pilot we usually do hosted with a temporary reserved for the bench runs.
[03:42] Priya: on security side we need SOC2, SAML SSO, and ability to keep logs in our VPC. is that supported for pilot?
[03:49] Maya: yes - Redwood Private supports VPC and auditing; for the hosted POC we can enable audit logs and SSO, and we have a security pack we can share. we'll attach the SOC2/ISO certs.

[03:58] Arjun: back to benchmarking - telemetry we need: request id, prompt length, response length, batch size, model variant, quant flag, latency p50/p95/p99, token counts and compute ms per token. even a CSV with those fields will be enough for our cost model.
[04:15] Lena: ok we'll pull a week's worth of request traces, obfuscate PII and share.
[04:18] Speaker 1: question - do you have a recommended sample rate for traces?
[04:21] Arjun: 100% for a week is ideal but 10% stratified across peak/steady is workable. include any long-form cases.

[04:30] Mark: curious about fallback/routing - if we miss SLOs can we automatically route to cheaper model to maintain availability?
[04:36] Maya: yes, Redwood supports policy routing: route by latency or cost tier, and we can set automatic fallback to a smaller model when latency breaches or when capacity is limited. that helps availability but will change model output quality so product will want to examine degraded outputs.
[04:50] Lena: we will want a manual canary first then auto after we accept quality delta.

[04:55] Arjun: small note on batching: for low-latency interactive we usually keep batch size small (1-4) to hit p95 targets; larger sizes give lower per-token compute but increase tail latency. part of the bench is to quantify the knee.
[05:08] Priya: any network egress concerns with hosted? we prefer keeping customer content in region.
[05:12] Maya: hosted runs in region options, and for pilot we can spin a region nearest you. private offers full VPC but that's more setup time.

[05:20] Mark: timeline outline?
[05:22] Noah: propose week 0: data and prompts exchanged, week 1 bench setup and initial runs, week 2 knob sweeps and prefix cache simulation, week 3 final run and extrapolated economics and decision. we can compress to 2 weeks if you give live access.
[05:36] Lena: 3 week is fine, want final report with per-1k token cost vs p95 chart and recommended production config.
[05:44] Maya: yep we'll deliver a cost spreadsheet with scenarios: baseline, 20%/40% cache hit, quantized savings, reserved vs hosted, and a recommended config with expected monthly cost at your 25k requests/mo estimate and for scale scenarios (100k/mo).

[05:58] Arjun: i'll also include a bench plan doc and a reproducible script. We'll capture p50/p95/p99 and token economics.
[06:04] Speaker 1: are you able to show me sample output quality diff between the high-quality and 3B model?
[06:08] Arjun: yes we can include side-by-side samples and a short quality rubric for product to score. that's part of deliverables.

[06:15] Mark: for acceptance criteria we propose: 1) cost under pilot budget extrapolated to production with stated assumptions, 2) p95 latency under 500ms (400ms preferred), 3) quality delta acceptable vs baseline per product rubric.
[06:29] Lena: sounds good. also add security checklist item: ensure logs retention and SSO validated.

[06:35] Maya: recapping next steps quickly: 1) Maya to send cost model and security pack; 2) Lena to upload traces and sample prompts; 3) Arjun to schedule bench + provide script; 4) Noah coordinate calendar and finalize pilot timeline - target final deliverable week of 10/20.
[06:54] Priya: one more Q: if we hit an unexpected token spike during pilot how do you throttle?
[06:58] Arjun: we have rate limit policies and can set graceful degradation to smaller model and circuit-break to queue. we'll add instrumentation to alert when spend rate approaches thresholds.
[07:10] Maya: ok thanks all, we'll follow up in email with attachments.
[07:14] Lena: thanks, talk soon

End of transcript.
